name: Can an attached ADU be built without losing the character of the main house?

mainEntity.name: How can the addition match the existing home so it does not look like a bolted-on box?
mainEntity.text: How can the addition match the existing home so it does not look like a bolted-on box?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-designed attached ADU should feel like it belongs to the original house. That usually means matching or complementing roof pitch, siding, stucco texture, window proportions, trim details, and exterior color palette. The transition between old and new is especially important on visible street-facing or side-yard elevations, where mismatched forms can make the addition look tacked on. Good design also considers massing so the ADU does not overpower the original home. Some homeowners want a seamless match, while others prefer a subtle contemporary contrast; both can work if the proportions are handled carefully. The most successful projects maintain the architectural character of the neighborhood while still making the addition clearly functional. This question is often overlooked in generic ADU content, but it matters a lot for curb appeal and resale value. A luxury-focused design and construction team should be able to balance code compliance with architectural continuity.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a well-designed attached ADU can match the main home by aligning rooflines, materials, windows, proportions, and exterior details. The best projects look like a natural extension of the house rather than an afterthought.
